parsed.title: Discussion on AI in Job Search and Development

topics.title: AI tools for job searching and résumé generation

claims.text: The author plans to set up an automated system (OpenClaw) to find job vacancies, generate PDFs of tailored résumés, and write cover letters.
Knowledge of AI technologies (Cursor, Claude Code, LLM, RAG, embeddings) is increasingly required by recruiters in 2026.
The author expects the recruiter profession to disappear, favoring HR for personnel management.
Since 2025, AI tools have significantly accelerated development speed, allowing developers to generate complex queries and code quickly.
AI can replace routine tasks such as writing JOIN queries, leading to faster iteration and earlier detection of missing details.

topics.title: Risks of AI‑generated code and queries

claims.text: A colleague generated a 450‑line raw SQL query that fetched almost all data, causing potential security and performance issues (10‑20 min production queries).
The same AI‑generated code was later deemed unusable and was dropped after code review.
AI struggles with deep contextual understanding and cannot replace an experienced engineer's knowledge of optimizations, caching, and normalization.
Log analysis via AI was attempted but deemed unnecessary for the immediate bug‑fix task.

topics.title: Cultural perception of AI over time

claims.text: In 2024 AI was viewed dismissively, whereas by 2026 it is accepted as mainstream.
Comments suggest that the pace of technological change feels similar to past eras (REST, JSON, Docker).
